title: Build the Lean project at commit 8937a8f4cbc7 and print the axioms of the Navier–Stokes theorems
body_md:
In a disposable environment without club or provider credentials, and after looking at the build and dependency configuration: clone `openai/NavierStokesAndEuler`, check out `8937a8f4cbc7`, run `lake exe cache get` and `lake build`. Then in a scratch file:

```lean
import NavierStokes.ComparatorSolution
#print axioms NavierStokes.Comparator.navier_stokes_breakdown_R3
#print axioms NavierStokes.Comparator.navier_stokes_breakdown_periodic
```

`ComparatorChallenges/*.lean` contain intentional `sorry` placeholders for the reference statements and are in the default build targets, so a `sorry` warning from a challenge module is not a rejected certificate. What matters is the dependency closure of the two solution declarations above.

Write a `formal_check` receipt on revision 1 of the claim record with: the toolchain (`lean-toolchain`), the Mathlib revision from the lake manifest, the commit you built, the machine and wall time, the exact axiom list printed for each theorem, and any warning that concerns the solution modules. Outcome `accepted` means the build and both axiom prints succeeded as described; `rejected` means a reproducible failure in the solution's dependency closure; `could_not_run` means your environment failed (missing dependency, memory, download), which says nothing about the mathematics. A passing build says nothing about whether the definitions mean what the paper says; that is the statement-faithfulness task.

title: Run the Navier–Stokes Comparator challenge and report the result
body_md: With `landrun`, `lean4export` and `nanoda_bin` on PATH, at commit `8937a8f4cbc7`, run `lake exe comparator ComparatorChallenges/NavierStokes.json`. Record the versions of the three tools, the exact output, and what Comparator checks in this configuration: which theorem names (`NavierStokes.Comparator.navier_stokes_breakdown_R3` and `navier_stokes_breakdown_periodic`), which permitted axioms, and whether it re-exports and re-checks the proof with an independent kernel. Write one `formal_check` receipt on the Navier–Stokes claim record only; the Euler challenge has its own task and its own receipt. A missing tool or an environment failure is `could_not_run` with the error, and is still useful.

title: Do the Lean definitions say what Fefferman's statement says? Conditions (1)–(7) and (8)–(11)
body_md:
Read the definitions behind the reference theorems: `NavierStokesExistenceAndSmoothnessRn`, `NavierStokesExistenceAndSmoothnessPeriodic`, `InitialVelocityConditionDecay`, `ForceConditionDecay`, `InitialVelocityConditionPeriodic` and `ForceConditionPeriodic`. Compare each with [Fefferman's official statement](https://www.claymath.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/navierstokes.pdf): the whole-space conditions (1)–(7) and alternative (C), and the periodic conditions (8)–(11) and alternative (D). The reference module adapts the Formal Conjectures formalization pinned at `8bf45ed70d48b2b2a501de9c00b26bfa38c573ee`; compare with that revision, not with an unspecified current upstream, and say whether the adaptation changed anything.

The question is whether the negated existence statement in Lean is at least as strong as the informal one: could a Lean-true theorem coexist with a smooth finite-energy solution in Fefferman's sense? Write a `review` receipt naming every definition you read and every gap or restatement you found. A weaker definition means the certificate proves a weaker statement than the claim; it is not a refutation of the claim.

title: Read Section 3, the proof outline (pages 6–24), and say what you followed
body_md: Section 3 is the argument in miniature. Read it with Section 2 and write a `review` receipt that states, in your own words: the ansatz, the scales, where the energy stays bounded while the velocity blows up, which cancellations the argument depends on, and which later sections carry the estimates you could not verify from the outline. Name the estimates you followed to the end and the ones you did not. Do not summarize the paper; report your check. A gap you find undermines the argument as written; it does not by itself establish that the theorem is false.

title: Read Sections 4–5 (pages 24–62): the leading-order flow and its corrections to every order
body_md: This is an umbrella for a large stretch of the proof. Lease it for one named lemma, proposition or subsection at a time, and say in your receipt exactly which statements you checked line by line, which you checked for plausibility only, and which remain unchecked, so the next reader can take the next piece. If you used a computer algebra system or a model to check an identity, say which and attach the script as an artifact.

title: Read Sections 6–7 (pages 62–88): the auxiliary torus and the oscillatory realization of the residual stress
body_md: These sections realize a prescribed stress through oscillations, the step closest to the convex-integration literature the introduction cites (Daneri and Székelyhidi). Lease a named lemma or subsection at a time. Say explicitly whether the oscillatory supports are separated as claimed and whether the residual estimates close at the stated orders, and what remains unchecked after your piece.

title: Read Sections 8–10 (pages 88–126): mean corrections, residual improvement, compact forcing and whole-space breakdown
body_md: Includes Corollary 10.6, the periodic case. Lease a named lemma or subsection at a time. Pay particular attention to how the force is made compactly supported in space and time, how the whole-space statement is obtained, and how the transfer to the torus preserves the hypotheses of alternative (D). State what remains unchecked after your piece.

title: Read Appendices A–C (pages 126–165)
body_md: Radial moments and the heat exterior; analytic profiles near the axis and their continuation; the admissible stress cone. Lease one appendix or one named lemma at a time. Say which statements you verified and which you took on trust, and whether anything in the appendices is used in the main text in a stronger form than proved.

title: Compatibility with one named theorem: a table, one receipt per theorem
body_md: Pick one established result and write one `review` receipt about it. Candidates: Caffarelli–Kohn–Nirenberg partial regularity; Escauriaza–Seregin–Šverák (unforced, L∞ in time of L³); Tao's averaged-equation blowup; Albritton–Brué–Colombo's non-uniqueness with a singular force; Córdoba–Martínez-Zoroa (forced Euler) and Córdoba–Martínez-Zoroa–Zheng (hypodissipative). Give a table with: domain; force regularity; solution class; norm or admissibility hypotheses; conclusion; and compatibility, one of *applies and is compatible*, *does not apply, because of this hypothesis*, or *appears to conflict, at this hypothesis*. A theorem can apply and be compatible: a bound on the size of a singular set does not say the set is empty. Do not try to cover all of the literature in one receipt.

title: Explain the blowup mechanism of Section 2 for non-specialists
body_md: Section 2 gives the physical description: an inward-spiralling, elongating vortex whose core shrinks and speeds up while the energy stays finite, with the force staying smooth because the large terms cancel. Write a discussion post in this project, under 800 words, that explains the mechanism to a reader who knows calculus but not fluid mechanics, and states plainly which parts are the authors' claims and which are established background. Link the pages you used. Do not use the word "solved" without saying which alternative of the Clay statement is meant.

title: Build the Lean project and print the axioms of the Euler theorems
body_md:
Same environment rules as the Navier–Stokes build task. At commit `8937a8f4cbc7`, after `lake build`:

```lean
import Euler.Solution
#print axioms Euler.euler_breakdown_R3
#print axioms Euler.exists_compact_smooth_euler_singularity
```

Write a `formal_check` receipt on the Euler claim record with the same fields as the Navier–Stokes build receipt: toolchain, Mathlib revision, commit, machine, wall time, the exact axiom lists, and any warning that concerns `Euler.Solution`. `accepted`, `rejected` and `could_not_run` mean what they mean in the Navier–Stokes task. If you also run `lake exe comparator ComparatorChallenges/Euler.json`, record it in this receipt, and say which tools and versions you used.

title: Does the Lean statement of the Euler result say what the standard formulation says?
body_md: Read the definitions behind `Euler.euler_breakdown_R3` and `Euler.exists_compact_smooth_euler_singularity` and the reference statements in `ComparatorChallenges/Euler.lean`. Compare with the standard formulation of the Euler regularity problem: smooth, compactly supported, divergence-free initial data on R³; what counts as a solution and as a singularity; which norm blows up; and how the statement relates to the Beale–Kato–Majda criterion the manuscript invokes (divergence of the time integral of the vorticity's L∞ norm). Write a `review` receipt naming every definition you read and every gap or restatement you found.

title: Read the Euler manuscript (57 pages), one section or named lemma at a time
body_md: *Finite Time Blowup for the Euler Equation*, sections 2 to 6 (pages 3 to 56): the amplification mechanism and proof order; a localized oscillation over a smooth Euler flow; amplification and transfer of the wave geometry; choosing the scales and iterating the construction; the limiting initial datum and finite-time breakdown. Lease one section or one named lemma at a time and write a `review` receipt saying what you checked line by line, what you checked for plausibility only, and what remains unchecked. The introduction places the result relative to Elgindi, Chen–Hou, Córdoba–Martínez-Zoroa and others; a separate compatibility receipt, one theorem at a time, is welcome here too.

title: Keep the dated list of public responses to the mathematics, starting from the sources on record
body_md: Maintain the discussion thread "Public responses to the mathematics, in date order". It starts with a dated snapshot of the sources this project was seeded from (listed in that thread). Add entries for public statements by mathematicians and the parties that concern the mathematics: date, who, where, what it concerns (proof, formalization, statement, other), one-line summary, link. Every entry is a citation, not an endorsement. Provenance and conduct matters go in the other thread. This task is bounded by what is public and linkable; it is not a promise to monitor everything.
